question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have been working here for six months."'

options.A: He said that he had been working there for six months.
options.B: He said that he has been working here for six months.
options.C: He said that he was working there for six months.
options.D: He said that he had been working here for six months.

explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been working') backshifts to past perfect continuous ('had been working') after a past reporting verb ('said'), and 'here' shifts to 'there'.

question: Spot the error: 'The man asked me that why I was standing there.'

options.A: The man asked me
options.B: that why
options.C: I was standing there.
options.D: No error

explanation: In indirect WH-questions, 'that' is redundant and incorrect. Correct: 'The man asked me why I was standing there.'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'The supervisor said, "Finish this work immediately!"'

options.A: The supervisor ordered them to finish that work immediately.
options.B: The supervisor requested that they finish this work immediately.
options.C: The supervisor said that they should finish this work immediately.
options.D: The supervisor told to finish that work immediately.

explanation: Imperative commands convert using 'ordered/commanded' + object + full infinitive ('to finish'), with 'this' changing to 'that'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Alas! My father is no more."'

options.A: He exclaimed with sorrow that his father was no more.
options.B: He said that alas his father is no more.
options.C: He cried with joy that his father was no more.
options.D: He exclaimed that his father had been no more.

explanation: Exclamations of grief ('Alas!') use 'exclaimed with sorrow' and backshift 'is' to 'was'.

question: Spot the error: 'He told that he is waiting for his friend since morning.'

options.A: He told that
options.B: he is waiting
options.C: for his friend since morning.
options.D: No error

explanation: 'Tell' requires an indirect object (e.g., 'He told me that...'). Also, 'said' is safer if no object is provided. The tense 'is waiting' must backshift to 'was waiting' or 'had been waiting'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Can you speak French?"'

options.A: He asked me if I could speak French.
options.B: He asked me if I can speak French.
options.C: He asked whether I could speak French.
options.D: Both A and C are correct.

explanation: Both 'if' and 'whether' are correct conjunctions for yes/no questions in reported speech, and 'can' backshifts to 'could'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I have just come back."'

options.A: She said that she had just come back.
options.B: She said that she has just come back.
options.C: She said that she just came back.
options.D: She said that she would have just come back.

explanation: Present perfect ('have come') backshifts to past perfect ('had come').

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where did I live last year.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where did I live
options.C: last year.
options.D: No error

explanation: Indirect questions require declarative word order ('where I lived'), not interrogative ('where did I live').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Good morning, everyone!"'

options.A: He wished everyone good morning.
options.B: He told everyone good morning.
options.C: He said good morning to everyone.
options.D: Both A and C are correct.

explanation: Both 'wished' and 'said' are valid reporting verbs for greetings.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Must you go?"'

options.A: He asked if I had to go.
options.B: He asked if I must go.
options.C: He asked did I have to go.
options.D: He inquired whether I must go.

explanation: When 'must' denotes necessity, 'had to' is the preferred backshifted form.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Water freezes at 0 degrees."'

options.A: He said that water froze at 0 degrees.
options.B: He said that water freezes at 0 degrees.
options.C: He told that water freezes at 0 degrees.
options.D: He asked if water freezes at 0 degrees.

explanation: Scientific facts/universal truths remain in the present tense even if the reporting verb is past.

question: Spot the error: 'She said that she will submit her essay tomorrow.'

options.A: She said that
options.B: she will submit
options.C: her essay tomorrow.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb ('said') requires backshift of 'will' to 'would'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Bravo! You've done great."'

options.A: She applauded him, saying he had done great.
options.B: She exclaimed that he had done great.
options.C: She told him bravo for doing great.
options.D: She said that he has done great.

explanation: Bravo requires specific reporting expressions like 'applauded him' + reporting clause.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Let's eat."'

options.A: He proposed that they should eat.
options.B: He suggested eating.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Both gerund and 'should' clause structures are valid for suggestions.

question: Spot the error: 'The teacher told to the students to study hard.'

options.A: The teacher told to
options.B: the students to study hard.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: 'Tell' requires an indirect object without the preposition 'to'. Correct: 'The teacher told the students...'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I'll see you there."'

options.A: He said that he would see me there.
options.B: He said that he will see me there.
options.C: He said that he would see me here.
options.D: He told that he would see me there.

explanation: 'Will' -> 'would'. The location 'there' is usually kept if the report is at the same location as original, but contextually 'there' refers back.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Are you coming?"'

options.A: She asked if I was coming.
options.B: She asked was I coming.
options.C: She asked if I am coming.
options.D: She told me if I was coming.

explanation: Yes/no question 'if', declarative order 'I was', backshift 'are' -> 'was'.

options.C: No error
options.D: None

options.C: He said that he was there for hours.
options.D: He said that he had been here for hours.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Please pass the salt."'

options.A: She requested me to pass her the salt.
options.B: She told me to pass her the salt.
options.C: She asked me to pass her the salt.
options.D: All of the above are correct.

explanation: Reporting verbs like 'requested', 'told', and 'asked' can all be used for polite imperative requests.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I might visit them."'

options.A: He said that he might visit them.
options.B: He said that he may visit them.
options.C: He said that he would visit them.
options.D: He said that he had to visit them.

explanation: 'Might' is already past-like/conditional and usually remains unchanged.

explanation: Don't use 'that' before 'if'. Correct: 'He asked if I could help him.'
